title: Air India Extends Riyadh, Dammam Flight Suspensions to November 7
excerpt: IndiGo cancels all Saudi routes until October 31 and Akasa extends Riyadh to November 30, as passengers booked on or before October 24 get free rebooking or full refunds.
body:
• Air India and Air India Express have extended suspensions to Riyadh and Dammam until November 7, 2026, and to Jeddah until October 31, citing continued attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure.
  • IndiGo has cancelled flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 31, while Akasa Air has extended Jeddah suspensions to November 10 and Riyadh to November 30.
  • If your booking was issued on or before October 24, you can take a one-time free rebooking — for travel up to November 21 on Riyadh and Dammam routes and November 14 on Jeddah routes — or a full refund.
  • About 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have returned to India in the past week, the MEA said, with 24x7 embassy control rooms running in Riyadh and Jeddah.

Air India and Air India Express will keep flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam suspended until November 7, extending a halt that was due to end this weekend, as attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure continue. Services to and from Jeddah will remain suspended until October 31, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Saturday, confirming the airlines' joint advisory.

"In view of the prevailing situation in the region, Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 7 November 2026, while services to and from Jeddah will remain suspended until 31 October 2026," the airlines said in the advisory shared on X, according to ANI reporting of the Air India suspension advisory.

What Each Airline Is Doing

IndiGo has aligned its Saudi network to the same October 31 date. The airline first cancelled Riyadh flights until October 31 and Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah flights until October 27, then extended the three latter routes to October 31 as well. "The safety and well-being of our customers and crew continue to guide every decision we make. We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure safe operations," IndiGo said.

"The safety and well-being of our customers and crew continue to guide every decision we make."

— IndiGo, travel advisory

Akasa Air has gone further. On Friday it extended the suspension of its Jeddah flights until November 10 and its Riyadh flights until November 30, the longest halt announced by any Indian carrier on Saudi routes so far.

Your Rebooking and Refund Options

Passengers holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before October 24 qualify for flexible options. For Riyadh and Dammam, travellers with original travel dates up to November 7 may take a one-time complimentary rebooking to or from any operational Air India station in Saudi Arabia, subject to availability, for travel up to November 21. For Jeddah, travellers with original dates up to October 31 may rebook on the same terms for travel up to November 14, or cancel for a full refund. Air India Express passengers get a wider choice: rebooking through any operational station in Saudi Arabia or Bahrain. Full details are in the coverage of the extended suspension and passenger options. Check your booking before travelling to the airport, and keep the confirmation issued on or before October 24, because eligibility turns on that date.

https://x.com/airindia/status/2114047558612054112

Why Flights Are Grounded

The extensions follow continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including strikes on airports in Riyadh and Dammam and on Aramco's Shaybah oil field. India condemned the attacks on Thursday. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, one Indian national was killed and two were injured in the attack on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport, and another Indian was injured in the Shaybah strike.

Help for Stranded Travellers and Pilgrims

The disruption has hit Umrah pilgrims hardest. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said about 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have returned to India over the past week, and more than 10,000 regular Umrah pilgrims have also travelled back. The Indian Embassy and Consulate are running 24x7 control rooms in Riyadh and Jeddah, and the Consulate General in Jeddah is helping with food, essential medicines and onward bookings through community volunteers and tour operators. Travellers still in Saudi Arabia should stay in contact with their airline, tour operator and the nearest Indian mission, and follow embassy advisories rather than heading to the airport on a suspended route.

What Happens Next

Resumption now depends on the security picture, not airline scheduling. Jeddah is the first test, on October 31, followed by Riyadh and Dammam on November 7 for Air India, November 10 for Akasa's Jeddah route and November 30 for Akasa's Riyadh route. Anyone booked in November should treat those dates as provisional and confirm flight status close to departure.
